# Define functions for reading, processing, and plotting NUCmer alignments

The functions used to parse the NUCmer delta files and generate the plots were
adapted from the workflow available at the repository linked below.

Read Delta functions and plotting functions (adapted) used are from repository [here:](https://jmonlong.github.io/Hippocamplus/2017/09/19/mummerplots-with-ggplot2/)

The `readDelta()` function reads the alignment information contained in a
NUCmer delta file and converts the relevant alignment records into an R data
frame. For each alignment, the resulting table contains the reference start
and end coordinates, query start and end coordinates, reported alignment
error, reference sequence identifier, and query sequence identifier.

Reads in delta file output from nucmer into R and summaries into dataframe

```{r define-functions}

#===============================================================================
# Function: readDelta
#
# Purpose:
# Parse a delta file produced by NUCmer and return the principal coordinates
# and error values for each pairwise alignment block.
#
# Arguments:
#   deltafile  Path to a NUCmer delta file.
#
# Returns:
#   A data frame containing:
#     rs     Reference alignment start coordinate.
#     re     Reference alignment end coordinate.
#     qs     Query alignment start coordinate.
#     qe     Query alignment end coordinate.
#     error  Number of errors reported for the alignment.
#     qid    Query sequence identifier.
#     rid    Reference sequence identifier.
#     strand Orientation of the query alignment relative to the reference.
#===============================================================================

readDelta <- function(deltafile){
  # Read the complete delta file as individual text lines.
  lines = scan(deltafile, 'a', sep='\n', quiet=TRUE)

  # Remove the first line, which contains the paths or names of the input
  # sequences rather than an alignment record.
  lines = lines[-1]

  # Split each line into fields separated by spaces.
  lines.l = strsplit(lines, ' ')

  # Determine the number of fields present in each parsed line.
  lines.len = lapply(lines.l, length) %>% as.numeric

  # Remove single-field lines representing delta-encoded distance values.
  # The retained lines contain sequence headers or alignment summaries.
  lines.l = lines.l[lines.len != 1]
  lines.len = lines.len[lines.len != 1]

  # Identify sequence-header lines, which contain four fields.
  head.pos = which(lines.len == 4)

  # Associate each alignment record with the sequence header that precedes it.
  head.id = rep(head.pos, c(head.pos[-1], length(lines.l)+1)-head.pos)

  # Extract the seven numeric fields contained in each alignment-summary line.
  mat = matrix(as.numeric(unlist(lines.l[lines.len==7])), 7)

  # Retain the first five alignment fields and transpose them so that each
  # alignment occupies one row.
  res = as.data.frame(t(mat[1:5,]))

  # Assign informative column names to the retained alignment variables.
  colnames(res) = c('rs','re','qs','qe','error')

  # Recover the query sequence identifier associated with each alignment.
  res$qid = unlist(lapply(lines.l[head.id[lines.len==7]], '[', 2))

  # Recover the reference sequence identifier and remove the leading ">"
  # character from the delta header.
  res$rid = unlist(lapply(lines.l[head.id[lines.len==7]], '[', 1)) %>% gsub('^>', '', .)

  # Infer alignment orientation from the order of the query start and end
  # coordinates. Increasing coordinates represent the forward strand, whereas
  # decreasing coordinates represent the reverse orientation.
  res$strand = ifelse(res$qe-res$qs > 0, '+', '-')

  # Return the parsed alignment data frame.
  res
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: calculate_perc_id_mid_points
#
# Purpose:
# Calculate the reference length, approximate percentage identity, and
# reference and query midpoint of every NUCmer alignment.
#
# Arguments:
#   data  Data frame generated by readDelta().
#
# Returns:
#   The input data frame with additional columns describing alignment length,
#   percentage identity, identity category, and midpoint coordinates.
#===============================================================================

#calculates percentage identity and mid point for each mummer alignment
calculate_perc_id_mid_points <- function(data){
  # Calculate alignment length from the reference start and end coordinates.
  data$r_length <- (data$re - data$rs)

  # Estimate percentage identity using the reference alignment length and the
  # error count reported in the delta file.
  data$perc_id <- ((data$r_length - data$error)/data$r_length)*100

  # Create a copy of percentage identity for conversion to a categorical
  # variable where required by downstream plotting functions.
  data$perc_id_factor <- data$perc_id

  # Group alignments below 100% identity into a common category.
  data[data$perc_id < 100, "perc_id_factor"] <- "<100"

  # Convert the identity category to a factor.
  data$perc_id_factor <- as.factor(data$perc_id_factor)

  # Calculate the midpoint of each alignment on the reference sequence.
  data$r_mid <- (data$rs + data$re)/2

  # Calculate the midpoint of each alignment on the query sequence.
  data$q_mid <- (data$qs + data$qe)/2

  return(data)
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: pre_plot_analysis
#
# Purpose:
# Read a NUCmer delta file, calculate alignment summary statistics, and remove
# alignments shorter than a specified minimum reference length.
#
# Arguments:
#   delta_path  Path to the delta file.
#   min_size    Minimum retained alignment length in base pairs.
#
# Returns:
#   A processed and length-filtered alignment data frame.
#===============================================================================

#reads in delta file, calculates percentage ID and filters for a minimum alignment size
pre_plot_analysis <- function(delta_path, min_size = 20000){
  # Parse the NUCmer delta file.
  data = readDelta(delta_path)

  # Calculate alignment length, identity, and midpoint coordinates.
  data <- calculate_perc_id_mid_points(data)

  # Retain alignments whose reference length is at least min_size.
  data_filt <- data[data$r_length >= min_size,]

  return(data_filt)
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: plot_by_perc_id_cap
#
# Purpose:
# Produce a conventional NUCmer dot plot in which each alignment is represented
# as a segment from its reference coordinates to its query coordinates.
# Alignments are coloured according to percentage identity.
#
# Arguments:
#   data       Processed alignment data frame.
#   xmin       Lower reference-coordinate boundary.
#   xmax       Upper reference-coordinate boundary.
#   cap_lower  Lower limit of the percentage-identity colour scale.
#   cap_upper  Upper limit of the percentage-identity colour scale.
#===============================================================================

# Plots diagonal scatter plot of a nucmer pairwise alignment with points coloured by percentage identity of alignment - x axis is reference, y axis is query
plot_by_perc_id_cap <- function(data, xmin = 0, xmax = max(data$re), cap_lower, cap_upper){
  # Sort alignments by percentage identity so that the plotting order reduces
  # the effect of high-identity observations obscuring other alignments.

  #order data by % ID to help with overplotting
  data <- data[order(data$perc_id),]

  # Plot reference coordinates on the x axis and query coordinates on the
  # y axis. Each alignment is drawn as a segment and coloured by identity.
  ggplot(data[data$rs > xmin & data$re < xmax,], aes(x=rs, xend=re, y=qs, yend=qe, colour=perc_id)) + geom_segment() +
    geom_point(alpha=.5, size=1.5) +
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(strip.text.y=element_text(angle=180, size=5),
          strip.background=element_blank()) +
    xlab(unique(data$rid)) + ylab(unique(data$qid)) +
    scale_colour_viridis(limits = c(cap_lower, cap_upper)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(xmin,xmax,100000000)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,max(data$qe),100000000))
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: plot_by_perc_id_cap_midpoint
#
# Purpose:
# Plot the midpoint of each alignment rather than its complete alignment
# interval. Points are coloured by percentage identity. Axis labels and the
# legend are suppressed to facilitate use in a multi-panel figure.
#===============================================================================

plot_by_perc_id_cap_midpoint <- function(data, xmin = 0, xmax = max(data$re), cap_lower, cap_upper){
  # Sort observations by percentage identity before plotting.

  #order data by % ID to help with overplotting
  data <- data[order(data$perc_id),]

  # Plot the reference midpoint against the query midpoint for each alignment.
  ggplot(data[data$rs > xmin & data$re < xmax,], aes(x=r_mid, y=q_mid, colour=perc_id)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.3) +
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(strip.text.y=element_text(angle=180, size=5),
          strip.background=element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none",
          axis.title.x=element_blank(),
          axis.text.x=element_blank(),
          axis.title.y=element_blank(),
          axis.text.y=element_blank(),) +
    #xlab(unique(data$rid)) + ylab(unique(data$qid)) +
    scale_colour_viridis(limits = c(cap_lower, cap_upper)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(xmin,xmax,100000000)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,max(data$qe),100000000))+
    coord_cartesian(xlim=c(xmin,xmax))
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: plot_perc_id_v_ref
#
# Purpose:
# Plot alignment percentage identity against the alignment midpoint on the
# reference sequence. Point colour represents alignment length.
#===============================================================================

plot_perc_id_v_ref <- function(data, xmin = 0, xmax = max(data$re), ymin = 97, ymax = 100){
  # Restrict observations to the requested reference-coordinate interval and
  # plot identity as a function of reference position.
  ggplot(data[data$r_mid > xmin & data$r_mid < xmax,], aes(x=r_mid, y=perc_id, colour=r_length)) +
    theme_bw() + xlab(data$rid) + ylab(paste0('percentage ID v ', data$qid)) +
    geom_point(alpha=.5) +
    ylim(ymin, ymax) +
    scale_colour_viridis()
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: plot_perc_id_v_ref_no_length
#
# Purpose:
# Plot percentage identity against reference position without mapping alignment
# length to point colour. Axis titles, labels, and the legend are suppressed
# so that the plot can be incorporated into a composite figure.
#===============================================================================

plot_perc_id_v_ref_no_length <- function(data, xmin = 0, xmax = max(data$re), ymin = 97, ymax = 100, breaks = 0.5){
  ggplot(data[data$r_mid > xmin & data$r_mid < xmax,], aes(x=r_mid, y=perc_id)) +
    theme_bw() + 
    #xlab(data$rid) + 
   #ylab(paste0('percentage ID v ', data$qid)) +
    theme(strip.text.y=element_text(angle=180, size=5),
          strip.background=element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none",
          axis.title.x=element_blank(),
          axis.text.x=element_blank(),
          axis.title.y=element_blank(),
          axis.text.y=element_blank(),) +
    geom_point(alpha=.5, size = 0.5, colour = "gray25") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(xmin,xmax,100000000)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(ymin, ymax), breaks=seq(ymin,ymax,breaks)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim=c(xmin,xmax))
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: bin_data
#
# Purpose:
# Assign each alignment to a fixed-width genomic bin according to its midpoint
# on the reference sequence.
#
# Arguments:
#   data            Processed alignment data.
#   bin_size        Width of each genomic bin in base pairs.
#   max_chrom_size  Maximum chromosome coordinate included in the binning.
#===============================================================================

#bins alignment dataframe by reference position
bin_data <- function(data, bin_size, max_chrom_size){
  # Generate bin-end coordinates from zero to the specified chromosome size.
  bins <- seq(0, max_chrom_size, by = bin_size)

  # Initialise an empty bin assignment for every alignment.
  data$bin <- NA

  # Assign each reference midpoint to the corresponding genomic bin.
  for (i in bins){
    data$bin <- ifelse(((data$r_mid > (i-bin_size)) & (data$r_mid < (i-1))), i, data$bin)
  }

  return(data)
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: plot_medians_line_colour_cut_off
#
# Purpose:
# Summarise percentage identity within fixed-width reference bins and plot the
# median identity for each bin. Points are classified according to whether the
# median identity meets a specified identity threshold.
#===============================================================================

#plots median percentage identity of each bin against reference position, colour of point is based on if the median percentage identity passes the identity threshold
plot_medians_line_colour_cut_off <- function(data, bin_size = 10000000, cut_off = 99.99, ymin = 97, ymax = 100, max_chrom_size){
  # Assign alignments to genomic bins.
  comparison_filt_bin <- bin_data(data, bin_size = bin_size, max_chrom_size = max_chrom_size)

  # Calculate median alignment identity within each bin.
  comparison_medians <- aggregate(perc_id ~ bin, data = comparison_filt_bin, FUN=median)

  # Rename the summary column to describe its contents.
  colnames(comparison_medians)[2] <- "perc_id_median"

  # Initialise the identity-threshold classification.
  comparison_medians$cut_off <- NA

  # Classify each bin according to whether its median identity is above or
  # below the specified threshold.
  comparison_medians$cut_off <- ifelse(comparison_medians$perc_id >= cut_off, paste0(">=",cut_off), paste0("<",cut_off))
  comparison_medians$cut_off <- as.factor(comparison_medians$cut_off)
  
  # Plot median percentage identity against reference-bin position.
  ggplot(comparison_medians, aes(x=bin, y = perc_id_median, colour = cut_off)) +
    geom_line(colour = "grey") + 
    geom_point(size = 1)  + 
    ylim(ymin,ymax) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#73D055FF", "#440154FF")) +
    labs(colour = "% id") +
    theme_bw() +
    xlab(data$rid) +
    
    ggtitle(paste0(data$rid, " v ", data$qid, " BinSize: ", bin_size, " CutOff: ", cut_off))
}


#===============================================================================
# Function: plot_boxplots_median_colour_cut_off
#
# Purpose:
# Display the distribution of alignment percentage identities within genomic
# bins. Boxplot fill represents whether the median identity of a bin meets the
# specified identity threshold.
#===============================================================================

#plots boxplots of percentage identity of each bin against reference position, colour of boxplot is based on if the median percentage identity passes the identity threshold
plot_boxplots_median_colour_cut_off <- function(data, bin_size = 10000000, cut_off = 99.99, ymin = 97, ymax = 100, max_chrom_size){
  # Assign each alignment to a genomic bin.
  comparison_filt_bin <- bin_data(data, bin_size = bin_size, max_chrom_size = max_chrom_size)

  # Calculate median identity within each bin.
  comparison_medians <- aggregate(perc_id ~ bin, data = comparison_filt_bin, FUN=median)

  # Rename the median-identity column.
  colnames(comparison_medians)[2] <- "perc_id_median"

  # Initialise and assign the identity-threshold category.
  comparison_medians$cut_off <- NA
  comparison_medians$cut_off <- ifelse(comparison_medians$perc_id >= cut_off, paste0(">=",cut_off), paste0("<",cut_off))
  comparison_medians$cut_off <- as.factor(comparison_medians$cut_off)
  
  # Join bin-level median classifications back to the individual alignments.
  comparison_to_plot <- merge(comparison_filt_bin, comparison_medians)
  
  # Plot the identity distribution within each genomic bin.
  ggplot(comparison_to_plot, aes(x=bin, y = perc_id, group = bin, fill = cut_off)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, lwd = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkorchid4", "gold")) +
    #labs(fill = "% id") +
    #scale_colour_viridis() +
    #xlab(data$rid) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(strip.text.y=element_text(angle=180, size=5),
          strip.background=element_blank(),
          legend.position = "none",
          axis.title.x=element_blank(),
          axis.text.x=element_blank(),
          axis.title.y=element_blank(),
          axis.text.y=element_blank(),) +
    #ggtitle(paste0(data$rid, " v ", data$qid, " BinSize: ", bin_size, " CutOff: ", cut_off)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,max(data$re),100000000)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(ymin,ymax),breaks=seq(ymin,ymax,0.5))
}


## END OF FUNCTIONS
```


# Adjust the size of points in the dot plot

The `plot_by_perc_id_cap()` function is redefined below with a smaller point
size. The smaller points reduce overplotting when many alignment blocks occupy
similar positions in the dot plot. The alignment segments and all other
plotting settings remain unchanged.

**How to change the size of the points in geom_point() to a smaller one?** in the plotting function, Done below

```{r}

#===============================================================================
# Revised function: plot_by_perc_id_cap
#
# This version uses a point size of 0.4 rather than 1.5 to improve visualisation
# of dense NUCmer alignments.
#===============================================================================

plot_by_perc_id_cap <- function(data, xmin = 0, xmax = max(data$re), cap_lower, cap_upper){
  # Sort alignments by percentage identity before plotting.

  #order data by % ID to help with overplotting
  data <- data[order(data$perc_id),]

  # Draw complete alignment segments and overlay small semi-transparent points.
  ggplot(data[data$rs > xmin & data$re < xmax,], aes(x=rs, xend=re, y=qs, yend=qe, colour=perc_id)) + geom_segment() +
    geom_point(alpha=.5, size=0.4) +
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(strip.text.y=element_text(angle=180, size=5),
          strip.background=element_blank()) +
    xlab(unique(data$rid)) + ylab(unique(data$qid)) +
    scale_colour_viridis(limits = c(cap_lower, cap_upper)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(xmin,xmax,100000000)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,max(data$qe),100000000))
}
```


# Apply the workflow to Watkins and pangenome chromosome 5B alignments

This section iterates over NUCmer alignments between WATDE0042 and selected
wheat pangenome or Watkins assemblies. The analysis is restricted to
alignments of at least 10 kb within the first 20 Mb of chromosome 5B.

The 10 kb minimum alignment threshold was selected to reduce the contribution
of short matches, including matches that may arise from non-syntenic repetitive
elements. Dot plots are written individually as PDF files.

Adapting this section to alignments am working with.

#=========================================================================================
### For loop for CS v1.0 chr5B against chr5B of watkins assemblies W-0042 and W-0100

#=========================================================================================

```{r}

  # length, without restricting query coordinates.
  #filt_data <- comparison_filt %>%  filter(rs >= ref_start) %>% filter(re <= ref_end) %>% filter(r_length >= min_size)
  filt_data <- comparison_filt %>%  filter(rs >= ref_start) %>% filter(re <= ref_end) %>% filter(qs >= ref_start) %>% filter(qe <= ref_end) %>% filter(r_length >= min_size)


  # Construct and explicitly print the dot plot. Explicit printing is required
  # because the plotting command is evaluated inside a loop while a PDF device
  # is open.
  print(filt_data %>% plot_by_perc_id_cap(., cap_lower = 97, cap_upper = 100) + 

    # Rotate reference-axis labels and adjust their text size to improve
    # readability when coordinates are densely spaced.
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5 )) +

    # Reduce query-axis label size.
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4.5)) +

    # Display query coordinates in megabases at 100 Mb intervals and label the
    # axis with the query assembly and chromosome, hence divide by 1e8
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$qs), max(filt_data$qs), 1e6),labels = function(x) scales::number(x / 1e6, accuracy = 0.01),name = paste0(query, " ", chrom, " (Mb)")) +

    # Display reference coordinates in megabases at 100 Mb intervals and label
    # the axis with the reference accession and chromosome.
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$rs), max(filt_data$rs), 1e6),labels = function(x) scales::number(x / 1e6, accuracy = 0.01),name = paste0(ref, " ", chrom, " (Mb)")) +

    # Alternative axis formatting that displays raw base-pair coordinates with
    # comma separators.
    #scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$qs),max(filt_data$qs) ,1000000), labels = scales::comma, name = paste0(query, " ", chrom)) +
    #scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$rs),max(filt_data$rs) ,1000000), labels = scales::comma, name = paste0(ref, " ", chrom)) +

    # Historical examples of vertical markers for specific gene coordinates.
    #add a vline to the position of the gene on either genome
    #geom_vline(xintercept = 635597602, colour="red", lwd=0.3) +
    #geom_vline(xintercept = 635601741, colour="red", lwd=0.3) +

    # Add vertical lines at 10 Mb and 12.5 Mb on the WATDE0042 reference axis.
    # These coordinates delimit the first locus of interest in WATDE0042.

    # 🔴 Add horizontal/vertical lines at 10 Mb and 12.5 Mb - for W-0042 loc 1, and for wat0100 14.4e6, 15.1e6
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(9.1e6, 13.2e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +

    # Alternative WATDE0042 coordinates for a second locus retained as a
    # commented plotting option.
      # loc 2
    #geom_vline(xintercept = c(75.5e6, 75.8e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +
      
    # Alternative query-coordinate boundaries for WATDE0100.
      #watde0100
    #geom_hline(yintercept = c(13.9e6, 16.2e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) + 

    # Alternative query-coordinate boundaries for Norin 61.
      #norin61
   # geom_hline(yintercept = c(8.5e6, 11.5e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +

    # Alternative query-coordinate boundaries for Lancer.
          #lancer
    #geom_hline(yintercept = c(9.4e6, 10.3e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +
     
    # Add a descriptive title identifying the reference, query, chromosome,
    # and minimum retained alignment length.
    ggtitle(label = paste0("Dot plot of ",ref," ",chrom," against ",chrom, " of ",query, " alignments longer than ",min_size," bp")) +

    # Set the title text size.
    theme(plot.title=element_text(size=12))+

    # Add a subtitle reporting the plotted chromosome interval in megabases.
    #labs(subtitle=paste0("alignments between ",ref_start_mb,"-",ref_end_mb," Mb")) +

    # Set the subtitle text size.
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size=9)))
  
  # Close the current PDF graphics device and complete writing of the figure.
  dev.off()
 }
}
```

#=========================================================================================
### For loop for watkins assemblies W-0042 and W-0100  against PGs for 1-100 Mb 
#### October 14 2025
#=========================================================================================

When running `ggplot2` commands within a `for` loop, the plot object must be
explicitly passed to `print()` for it to be rendered on an open graphical
device. Without `print()`, the resulting PDF file may be empty.

```{r}

#===============================================================================
# Input and output configuration
#===============================================================================

# Define the directory containing the NUCmer delta files. Delta filenames are
# expected to follow the pattern:
#
#   <reference>_<query>.delta
#
base_dir <- "/Users/waweru/Documents/2022/IBSpy_Targets/2024-12-05_5B_Yellow_Rust/2025-07-02_Watkins_assemblies/nucmerResults/"

# Use a minimum alignment-length threshold of 10 kb. This threshold was chosen
# to reduce the contribution of short alignments that may represent matches
# between non-syntenic retrotransposons.

# now using a threshold of 10kb alignments, based on lit that excluding shorter alignments 
#between non-syntenic retro-transposons which have a median size of 9584 bp in wheat

# Define a percentage-identity threshold for functions that classify alignment
# summaries. This variable is not directly used in the dot-plot loop below.
cut_off <- 99.99

##create directory to save the plots

# Construct the directory in which generated PDF figures will be stored.
plot_dir <-  paste0(base_dir,"2026-06-19_dotPlotFigs/")

# Create the figure directory if it does not already exist. Suppress warnings
# when the directory is already present and assign the specified permissions.
dir.create(path = paste0(plot_dir), showWarnings = FALSE, mode = 0777)

# Record the current date so that it can be incorporated into output filenames
# and provide a record of when each figure was generated.

# to be added to figure as they are saved for posterity
date <- Sys.Date() 
date


#===============================================================================
# Plotting configuration
#===============================================================================

# Load scales for formatting chromosome coordinates displayed on plot axes.
# Coordinates are subsequently converted from base pairs to megabases.
library(scales) # to add commas to the axes labels

# Disable scientific notation where possible so that large genomic coordinates
# are displayed as conventional numbers.
options(scipen = 999) # to remove exponential numbers in the axes


#===============================================================================
# Chromosome and assembly identifiers
#===============================================================================

### starting the loop here, as we iterate over references

# Define the chromosome being analysed and construct the chromosome label used
# in figure titles and axis labels.
chr <- "5B"
chrom <- paste0("chr", chr)

# Define the genome assemblies compared against WATDE0042. These names must
# correspond to the query component of the delta filenames.

# the are the references being used 
queries <- c("kariega_v1","fielder_v1","renan_v2.1","paragon_v3","cadenza_v2","symattis","chinesespring","arinalrfor","jagger","julius","lancer","landmark","norin61","mace","stanley","WATDE0100")

# Define the NUCmer reference accession. In this analysis, WATDE0042 is used as
# the reference for all pairwise comparisons.

# these are the queries
references  <- c("WATDE0042") #, "WATDE0100")

# Historical variables retained as comments from an earlier version of the
# plotting workflow.

# this the reference,
#variety <- "chinese"

#ref <- "Chinese-Spring"


#===============================================================================
# Iterate over pairwise comparisons
#===============================================================================

# Process every combination of query and reference listed above.
for (query in queries) {
  
  for (ref in references) {

  # Construct the path to the NUCmer delta file for the current comparison.
  data_dir_query <- paste0(base_dir,ref,"_",query,".delta")

  # Print the input path to the rendered report or R console to document which
  # comparison is being processed.
  print(data_dir_query)
  
  ## read in the data

  # Set the minimum retained alignment length to 10,000 bp.
  min_size <- 10000

  # Parse the delta file, calculate alignment statistics, and retain alignments
  # meeting the minimum-length requirement.
  comparison_filt <- pre_plot_analysis(delta_path = data_dir_query, min_size = min_size)
  
  #plot and save 
  #========================================================
  #===== plot based on filters for start and end region ======
  #===== alignments longer then 10kb, for a specific region ======

  # Define the chromosome interval displayed in the final dot plot. The current
  # analysis includes positions from 0 to 20 Mb on both the reference and query
  # sequences.
  ref_start <- 0
  ref_end <- 20000000

  # Restate the minimum alignment length used by the regional filter.
  min_size <- 10000
  
  # Convert the reference boundaries from base pairs to megabases for use in
  # output filenames, figure subtitles, and descriptive labels.

  ## divide by 1000000 to get values in <b for plotting
  ref_start_mb <- ref_start / 1e6
  ref_end_mb   <- ref_end / 1e6
  #min_size_mb <- min_size / 1e6


  # The commented TIFF command documents an alternative raster output format
  # used in an earlier version of the workflow.

#tiff(paste0(plot_dir,date,"_dot_plot",ref," _2B_VS_",query,"_","30-55Mbp",min_size,"bp.tiff"), res = 300, width = 8.3, height = 4.8, units = "in")

  # Open a PDF graphics device for the current comparison. The output filename
  # records the analysis date, reference, query, chromosome, and plotted
  # interval.
  pdf(paste0(plot_dir,date,"_",ref,"_v_",query,"_",chrom,"_", ref_start_mb,"-",ref_end_mb,"Mb_v2.pdf"), width = 10.4, height = 6.8)# res =   300, units = "in")
  
  # Alternative output filename that omits the plotted interval.
  #  pdf(paste0(plot_dir,date,"_",ref,"_v_",query,"_",chrom,".pdf"), width = 10.3, height = 6.8)# res =   300, units = "in")

  # Historical filtering expression retained as a comment.
  #%>% filter(rs >= 19000000) %>% filter(re <= ref_end)

  # Retain alignments entirely contained within the selected interval on both
  # the reference and query sequences. Also require a reference alignment
  # length of at least 10 kb.

# we filter start and end for both ref and query
  filt_data <- comparison_filt %>%  filter(rs >= ref_start) %>% filter(re <= ref_end) %>% filter(qs >= ref_start) %>% filter(qe <= ref_end) %>% filter(r_length >= min_size)

  # Alternative filter that restricts only reference coordinates and alignment
  # length, without restricting query coordinates.
  #filt_data <- comparison_filt %>%  filter(rs >= ref_start) %>% filter(re <= ref_end) %>% filter(r_length >= min_size)


  # Construct and explicitly print the dot plot. Explicit printing is required
  # because the plotting command is evaluated inside a loop while a PDF device
  # is open.
  print(filt_data %>% plot_by_perc_id_cap(., cap_lower = 97, cap_upper = 100) + 

    # Rotate reference-axis labels and adjust their text size to improve
    # readability when coordinates are densely spaced.
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5 )) +

    # Reduce query-axis label size.
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4.5)) +

    # Display query coordinates in megabases at 1 Mb intervals and label the
    # axis with the query assembly and chromosome.
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$qs), max(filt_data$qs), 1e6),labels = function(x) scales::number(x / 1e6, accuracy = 0.001),name = paste0(query, " ", chrom, " (Mb)")) +

    # Display reference coordinates in megabases at 1 Mb intervals and label

    #scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$rs), max(filt_data$rs), 1e6),labels = function(x) scales::number(x / 1e6, accuracy = 0.001),name = paste0(ref, " ", chrom, " (Mb)")) +
    #### changin scale x so that the x axis scale is always the same in all the plots
      
    scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(ref_start, ref_end),
    breaks = seq(ref_start, ref_end, by = 1e6),
    labels = function(x) scales::number(x / 1e6, accuracy = 1),
    name = paste0(ref, " ", chrom, " (Mb)"),
    expand = c(0, 0)) +
    # Alternative axis formatting that displays raw base-pair coordinates with
    # comma separators.
    #scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$qs),max(filt_data$qs) ,1000000), labels = scales::comma, name = paste0(query, " ", chrom)) +
    #scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(filt_data$rs),max(filt_data$rs) ,1000000), labels = scales::comma, name = paste0(ref, " ", chrom)) +

    # Historical examples of vertical markers for specific gene coordinates.
    #add a vline to the position of the gene on either genome
    #geom_vline(xintercept = 635597602, colour="red", lwd=0.3) +
    #geom_vline(xintercept = 635601741, colour="red", lwd=0.3) +

    # Add vertical lines at 10 Mb and 12.5 Mb on the WATDE0042 reference axis.
    # These coordinates delimit the first locus of interest in WATDE0042.

    # 🔴 Add horizontal/vertical lines at 10 Mb and 12.5 Mb - for W-0042 loc 1, and for wat0100 14.4e6, 15.1e6
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(9.1e6, 13.2e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +

    # Alternative WATDE0042 coordinates for a second locus retained as a
    # commented plotting option.
      # loc 2
    #geom_vline(xintercept = c(75.5e6, 75.8e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +
      
    # Alternative query-coordinate boundaries for WATDE0100.
      #watde0100
    #geom_hline(yintercept = c(14.4e6, 15.1e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) + 

    # Alternative query-coordinate boundaries for Norin 61.
      #norin61
   # geom_hline(yintercept = c(8.5e6, 11.5e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +

    # Alternative query-coordinate boundaries for Lancer.
          #lancer
    #geom_hline(yintercept = c(9.4e6, 10.3e6), colour = "red", lwd = 0.3) +
     
    # Add a descriptive title identifying the reference, query, chromosome,
    # and minimum retained alignment length.
    ggtitle(label = paste0("Dot plot of ",ref," ",chrom," against ",chrom, " of ",query, " alignments longer than ",min_size," bp")) +

    # Set the title text size.
    theme(plot.title=element_text(size=12))+

    # Add a subtitle reporting the plotted chromosome interval in megabases.
    labs(subtitle=paste0("alignments between ",ref_start_mb,"-",ref_end_mb," Mb")) +

    # Set the subtitle text size.
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size=9)))
  
  # Close the current PDF graphics device and complete writing of the figure.
  dev.off()
 }
```
